title: Do and Make: Actions, Things and Expressions
summary: Choose do for many actions and routine tasks, and make for creating or producing something. Practise common combinations such as do homework, make a mistake and take a photo.
learningObjectives: Distinguish general actions with do from producing or creating something with make.
Use do correctly in common expressions about study, work, household tasks and favours.
Use make correctly with mistakes, appointments, phone calls, lists, noise and beds.
Distinguish make a film from take a photo.

explanation.heading: Do for actions and tasks
explanation.body: Use do when you mean perform an action or complete a task without naming a particular thing you produce. Do can also stand in for an action that is already clear. The question “What do you do?” often asks about your job.
explanation.example: I have several things to do before our guests arrive.

explanation.heading: Make for things you create or produce
explanation.body: Use make when the action creates, prepares or produces something. You can make food, clothes or a simple object. Do and make are not interchangeable in every sentence.
explanation.example: We made some sandwiches for the train journey.

explanation.heading: Common expressions with do
explanation.body: Learn fixed combinations such as do homework, do housework, do the shopping, do an exercise, do a course, do a test and do someone a favour. When the verb changes tense, the expression stays together: do homework, did homework, have done homework.
explanation.example: Mira did the shopping while her partner cleaned the kitchen.

explanation.heading: Common expressions with make
explanation.body: Say make a mistake, make an appointment, make a phone call, make a list, make a noise and make your bed. These phrases use make even when no physical object is produced.
explanation.example: I made a list so I would not forget the ingredients.

explanation.heading: A useful contrast: films and photos
explanation.body: We make a film, but we normally take a photo or take a picture. Memorise the whole combination rather than choosing only by the meaning of the verb.
explanation.example: The students made a short film and took photos of the set.

comparisons.title: Doing a task versus making something

left.label: Do an activity
left.example: I did my homework after tea.
left.note: Do focuses on completing an activity or task.

right.label: Make something
right.example: I made a small model after tea.
right.note: Make focuses on creating an object.

left.label: Make a film
left.example: They made a film about their town.
left.note: Make is the usual verb for film production.

right.label: Take a photo
right.example: They took a photo of their town.
right.note: Take is the usual verb with a photo or picture.

examples.sentence: Could you do me a favour and close the window?
examples.note: Do someone a favour is a fixed phrase.

examples.sentence: I made an appointment with the dentist for Friday.
What do you do in the evenings?
examples.note: Do asks about activities in general.

examples.sentence: Please do not make a noise while the baby is asleep.
examples.note: Make a noise is a common expression.

examples.sentence: We did a short course and made a video together.
examples.note: Do a course, but make a video.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I need to make my homework now.
commonMistakes.correct: I need to do my homework now.
commonMistakes.why: Homework is an activity: use do homework.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Please do your bed before school.
commonMistakes.correct: Please make your bed before school.
commonMistakes.why: The fixed expression is make your bed.

commonMistakes.incorrect: He did a mistake in the report.
commonMistakes.correct: He made a mistake in the report.
commonMistakes.why: Use make a mistake, not do a mistake.

commonMistakes.incorrect: We made a photo of the waterfall.
commonMistakes.correct: We took a photo of the waterfall.
commonMistakes.why: Use take a photo for photographing something.

studyTips: Practise verb and noun together: do the washing-up, make a phone call and make a mistake.
When a phrase is new, check whether English normally pairs it with do, make or another verb.
Use past forms in short practice sentences: did homework, made lunch and took a photo.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: After dinner, we usually ___ the washing-up.
exercises.feedback: Do the washing-up is the fixed expression for washing dishes.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: The children ___ a paper boat in art class yesterday.
exercises.feedback: Made is the past of make; the children created a paper boat.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: You need to ___ an appointment before visiting this dentist.
exercises.feedback: Make an appointment is the usual expression for arranging a visit.

choices: Could you do me a favour?
Could you make me a favour?
Could you take me a favour?
exercises.feedback: Do someone a favour is a fixed expression.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the -ing form of do: My brother is ___ a cooking course this month.
acceptedAnswers: doing
exercises.feedback: The expression is do a course; after is, use doing.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the past form of make: I ___ a mistake in my email yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: made
exercises.feedback: The past form of make is made; we make a mistake.

exercises.prompt: Complete using do or make: Please ___ your bed before breakfast.
acceptedAnswers: make
exercises.feedback: Make your bed is a fixed expression.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the past form of do: We ___ the shopping last Saturday.
acceptedAnswers: did
exercises.feedback: Do the shopping becomes did the shopping in the past.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Sara made her homework before lunch.
acceptedAnswers: Sara did her homework before lunch.
exercises.feedback: Use do homework; did is the past tense.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Liam did a delicious cake for the party.
acceptedAnswers: Liam made a delicious cake for the party.
exercises.feedback: Making a cake means preparing or creating it.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I need to do a phone call before I leave.
acceptedAnswers: I need to make a phone call before I leave.
exercises.feedback: The fixed expression is make a phone call.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We made a photo of the garden.
acceptedAnswers: We took a photo of the garden.
exercises.feedback: Say take a photo, not make a photo, when you photograph a place.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say one complete sentence in the past from these cues: Noah / do / his homework / after lunch.
acceptedAnswers: Noah did his homework after lunch.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use did, the past of do, with homework.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say one complete sentence from these cues: I / need to / make / an appointment / tomorrow.
acceptedAnswers: I need to make an appointment tomorrow.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use the phrase make an appointment after need to.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say one complete sentence using the present continuous: Our neighbours / make / a cake / for the picnic.
acceptedAnswers: Our neighbours are making a cake for the picnic.
speakingExercises.feedback: Are making shows an action in progress; make a cake is the correct combination.

speakingExercises.prompt: Every Tuesday, Elena prepares a list of jobs. Begin with Elena and say one complete present-simple sentence using make a list of jobs and every Tuesday.
acceptedAnswers: Elena makes a list of jobs every Tuesday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Make a list is the natural combination. Use makes with the singular subject Elena.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change 'Omar does the shopping on Mondays.' into a negative present-simple sentence. Begin with Omar, keep on Mondays, and use doesn't or does not.
acceptedAnswers: Omar doesn't do the shopping on Mondays.
Omar does not do the shopping on Mondays.
speakingExercises.feedback: After does not or doesn't, use the base form do in the expression do the shopping.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend asks, 'What did you do during lunch?' You made a phone call to your cousin. Begin with I and give one sentence using made a phone call and during lunch.
acceptedAnswers: I made a phone call to my cousin during lunch.
speakingExercises.feedback: Made a phone call is the correct past-tense expression for this activity.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct this sentence using the past form of do, keeping all other words: 'Our class made a short course in photography last term.' Say the whole corrected sentence.
acceptedAnswers: Our class did a short course in photography last term.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use did a course, not made a course. Did is the past form of do.

speakingExercises.prompt: Tonight you must complete your homework and prepare a sandwich for tomorrow. Say one sentence beginning with Tonight, using will, do my homework and make a sandwich for tomorrow, in that order.
acceptedAnswers: Tonight, I will do my homework and make a sandwich for tomorrow.
Tonight, I'll do my homework and make a sandwich for tomorrow.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use do my homework for a task and make a sandwich for preparing food; will takes the base verbs do and make.

listeningExercises.audioText: Ella made a small wooden box in her art class.
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker says that Ella made a small wooden box.

listeningExercises.audioText: I do the washing-up after supper, and my brother dries the plates.
listeningExercises.prompt: What does the speaker do after supper?
listeningExercises.feedback: Doing the washing-up means washing the dishes.

listeningExercises.audioText: Please make your bed before you leave the house.
listeningExercises.prompt: Complete the expression you hear: “Please ___ your bed before you leave the house.” Type one word.
acceptedAnswers: make
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker uses make your bed.

listeningExercises.audioText: Nadia made a list of the food she needed before going to the market.
listeningExercises.prompt: What was Nadia preparing to do?
listeningExercises.feedback: She made a list of needed food before visiting the market, so she was getting ready to shop.

listeningExercises.audioText: Before the visitors arrived, Karim made two phone calls and then made the beds.
listeningExercises.feedback: The phone calls came first; he made the beds afterwards, before the visitors arrived.

listeningExercises.audioText: Rosa made a wooden chair for the classroom and did a safety test before anyone used it.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which sentence best describes Rosa's work?
choices: She only cleaned an old chair.
She built something and checked it.
She bought a chair without testing it.
listeningExercises.feedback: Made a chair means she created it; did a safety test means she checked it before use.

listeningExercises.audioText: After the lesson, Martin did a short maths test without his notes.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type only the past-tense verb heard immediately before 'a short maths test'.
acceptedAnswers: did
listeningExercises.feedback: Did is the past form in the expression do a test.

listeningExercises.audioText: I made a mistake when I copied the date into my diary.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word expression that means 'made an error' in the recording.
acceptedAnswers: made a mistake
listeningExercises.feedback: Made a mistake is the natural past-tense expression for making an error.
